Agent security is fundamentally a contextual problem.

Task Alignment specifies the agent's authorized objective.
Action Alignment evaluates whether each action serves the agent's authorized objective.
Data Isolation governs information flows across privilege boundaries.

Snapshot benchmarks are structurally incapable of evaluating Data Isolation.
Existing defenses can be reorganized around the property they actually approximate.

claims.text: The paper proposes temporal bridges with bidirectional alignment as a way to enhance climate data super-resolution.
High-resolution climate data is crucial for meteorological predictions.
The acquisition of high-resolution climate information is often prohibitively costly.
The high cost of acquiring high-resolution climate information necessitates the development of data-driven meteorological prediction models.
Climate data super-resolution (SR) is a process that generates fine-grained climate data from low-resolution inputs.
Recent deep learning advancements for climate data SR have primarily focused on leveraging single-frame spatial information.
Recent deep learning work for climate data SR has largely neglected the temporal correlations between different time frames.
Temporal correlations between different time frames could enhance climate data SR outcomes.
Climate data are inherently stochastic and noisy.
Widely used temporal alignment methods, such as optical flow models, are ineffective for climate data.
Developing a framework tailored for climate data SR that effectively captures implicit temporal correlations remains an unresolved challenge
The authors propose a novel Temporal-Enhanced framework with bidirectional temporal alignment.
The proposed framework establishes a temporal bridge to enhance spatial resolution in climate data SR through bidirectional alignment.
The proposed bidirectional alignment framework leads to improved SR performance.
Paired Latent Mapping achieves spatial alignment within the framework.
Bidirectional Temporal Alignment captures temporal correlations by training forward and backward networks on consecutive latent frames.
The Temporal Enhanced Super-resolution framework optimizes the entire framework for climate data super-resolution.
Experiments on large-scale real-world datasets were conducted.

The framework includes automated semantic evaluation of the extracted information against a gold standard.
The schema serves as an information model encoding domain knowledge.
The schema provides a unified, systematic, and consistent framework for extraction of hierarchical, nested information with attributes of va
The schema provides a unified, systematic, and consistent framework for evaluation of the extraction results.
Information extraction from a document is performed in a single call to the model, in zero-shot mode.
The authors introduce a path-based semantic matching algorithm to align nested, variable-cardinality attributes in the extracted results wit

The framework extracted 12 out of 14 attributes from documents published by the health technology assessment organisation NICE, using the ge
The framework achieved an F1 score of greater than 90% on the extraction of attributes from NICE documents.
The time needed to extract the attributes from a document was approximately 30 times lower than the time taken by a human domain expert.
The framework generalises across different generative AI models.

Search agents extend large language models beyond static parametric memory.
Search agents acquire and use external evidence during multi-step reasoning.
For knowledge-intensive tasks involving complex or evolving information, the reliability of search agents depends not only on retrieving rel
For knowledge-intensive tasks, the reliability of search agents also depends on using retrieved evidence to guide subsequent reasoning.
Existing methods primarily reward final-answer correctness or intermediate progress.
Existing methods do not directly assess whether post-retrieval actions are grounded in the retrieved evidence.
The misalignment between rewards and evidence grounding encourages prior-driven reasoning.
In prior-driven reasoning, agents form conclusions based on internal knowledge and use retrieval mainly to confirm them.
Prior-driven reasoning results in confirmation bias and inefficient evidence use.
The authors propose Contextual Information Policy Optimization (CIPO), an evidence-oriented reinforcement learning framework.
CIPO explicitly aligns policy optimization with external evidence use.
CIPO assigns dense, turn-level credit to reasoning actions influenced by retrieved information.
CIPO combines its evidence-use signal with a global outcome reward.
CIPO promotes reasoning trajectories in which retrieved facts can guide or revise subsequent reasoning.
CIPO requires neither human process annotations nor an additional reward model.
The experiments for CIPO covered seven in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks.
CIPO reduces the prevalence of prior-driven reasoning.
CIPO achieves excellent performance on most of the evaluated tasks.

claims.text: Robust aggregation methods are widely used in federated learning to mitigate the impact of adversarial client behavior.
Distance-based aggregation rules such as Krum and Multi-Krum select updates that are closest to the majority under the assumption that benig
Distance-based aggregation rules rely on geometric properties that can be exploited by adaptive adversaries.
The Krum-Proxy attack is a selection-aware backdoor injection strategy that consistently bypasses Byzantine-robust aggregation.
The Krum-Proxy method does not rely on naive scaling or naive constraining of malicious updates.
The Krum-Proxy method actively optimizes malicious updates to infiltrate the dense core of the benign distribution.
The Krum-Proxy method constructs adversarial updates that are similar to benign updates.
The Krum-Proxy method achieves its adversarial optimization through a two-stage optimization procedure that separates task-specific attack o
The Krum-Proxy method uses a nearest-neighbor proxy, stochastic reference modeling, and anchor-guided alignment in its optimization procedur
The Krum-Proxy method introduces a projection mechanism that constrains adversarial updates within realistic norm and variance bounds.
Krum-Proxy achieves higher attack success on standard federated learning benchmarks.
The vulnerability of distance-based aggregation to selection-aware adversaries is highlighted by the results of the Krum-Proxy experiments.

claims.text: Frontier AI models have knowledge that could be misused for nefarious purposes.
Frontier AI models' knowledge that could be misused for nefarious purposes poses a risk that needs to be addressed.
Gradient Routed Auxiliary Modules (GRAM) is a method for isolating dangerous knowledge to specific modules within a language model.
The modules isolating dangerous knowledge in a language model can be switched on or off to control what the model knows.
Switching the modules isolating dangerous knowledge on or off makes it possible to restrict or extend access to the most sensitive model cap
In the authors' experiments, a single model trained with GRAM can approximate multiple models, each trained with a different category of dan

The GRAM method has not been applied to production models at Anthropic.
The work introducing GRAM was done at AE Studio, in collaboration with Anthropic.
Misuse of legitimately helpful knowledge for harmful tasks, such as creating biological weapons or attacking critical infrastructure, is one
AI companies already manage the misuse risk from frontier AI models with a mix of defenses.
The defenses AI companies use against misuse include training models to refuse harmful requests.
The defenses AI companies use against misuse include running classifiers to detect and reject dangerous queries.
The defenses AI companies use against misuse include restricting which users can access which models through vetting and tiered deployment.
Each of the existing misuse defenses has drawbacks.
Refusals and classifiers are behavioral layers on top of knowledge the model still has.
Refusals and classifiers can be jailbroken.
Refusals and classifiers must be retuned for every model release.
Tiered access works at the level of whole models and whole accounts.
Tiered access forces a coarse trade-off: a user either gets every capability the model has, or gets a weaker model across the board.
An alternative to existing defenses is access control at the level of individual capabilities.
A deployment could include advanced virology knowledge for a vetted biosecurity lab while excluding it everywhere else, with general perform

GRAM approximates the performance of multiple data filtered models.
GRAM approximates the performance of multiple data filtered models at the cost of a single training run.
GRAM builds on prior ideas including DEMix layers, SGTM, and gradient routing.
The authors' contribution is to develop the prior ideas underlying GRAM for better performance.
The authors test GRAM in a larger and more realistic setting than prior work.
NULLs is a similar method that was developed concurrently with GRAM.
Post-hoc unlearning methods are designed to remove concepts from an existing model.
The authors compare GRAM against post-hoc unlearning methods.
LoRA is a competitive baseline that fine-tunes a filtered model to add dual use capabilities back in.

Switching a story topic off in the GRAM model performs similarly to training a model from scratch on data with that topic filtered out.

GRAM augments the MLP layer in each block of a Transformer by introducing small auxiliary modules, which are just additional neurons.
During training, the auxiliary modules that participate in forward and backward passes are chosen based on the data in each batch.
When training on dual use data, the corresponding auxiliary module is active for forward and backward passes.
When training on general-purpose "core" data, GRAM occasionally enables a random auxiliary module.

Ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) are conflicting affective states that precede the delay or abandonment of health behaviour change.
Recognition of ambivalence and hesitancy at the video level is difficult.
The signal of ambivalence and hesitancy arises from disagreement across and within facial, vocal, linguistic, and bodily modalities.
Ambivalence and hesitancy manifests differently across individuals.
PRISM-AH is a framework that treats ambivalence and hesitancy as a multimodal conflict that unfolds over time.
PRISM-AH encodes frozen vision, audio, and text encoders aligned into short time windows.
PRISM-AH passes the aligned time-window representations to a lightweight streaming model.
The lightweight streaming model scores cross-modal dissonance.
The lightweight streaming model predicts each next window to expose a hesitation surprise signal.
The lightweight streaming model discovers behaviour prototypes.
The lightweight streaming model is conditioned on participant metadata.
Dense window-level annotations supervise the PRISM-AH model as an auxiliary objective.
The PRISM-AH decision threshold is calibrated for macro F1.
A knowledge-guided large language model reasons over structured evidence using the expert cue taxonomy of the dataset.
The verdict of the knowledge-guided large language model is fused late into PRISM-AH only when validation performance improves.

The reported zero-shot baseline attains a macro F1 of 0.2827 on the labelled public test partition of 525 videos.

The reasoning gain of PRISM-AH is validated to transfer from the validation partition to the larger test partition.

claims.text: Medical Vision-Language Models (Med-VLMs) excel at verbalizing visual content.

Existing Med-VLM approaches verbalize regions as coordinate strings.
Existing approaches that decouple perception from understanding create representation gaps for region-language alignment.
MedUP is a Med-VLM that natively unifies perception and understanding within a shared token space.

UniMedTok enables the MedUP model to seamlessly interleave mask tokens with text.

claims.text: Large language models are increasingly deployed in education, healthcare, policy advising, and other interactive settings.
Users engage large language models as sustained social interlocutors rather than as one-shot query engines.
The shift toward sustained social interaction with large language models makes jailbreaks a growing safety threat.
Most research on jailbreaks emphasizes single-turn prompt optimization or iterative attack refinement.
Psychologically grounded multi-turn vulnerabilities of large language models are underexplored.
The authors present PsychJail, a psychology-guided framework for red teaming aligned large language models through theory-grounded, multi-tu
PsychJail maps established social-psychological persuasion techniques into a tactic-conditioned attack policy.
PsychJail factorizes each attacker action into a Change-of-Meaning analysis, tactic selection, and a victim-visible message.
PsychJail operationalizes the Persuasion Knowledge Model (PKM).
The PsychJail attack policy is refined with trajectory-level reinforcement learning using a PKM-gated reward.
The PKM-gated reward credits early jailbreak success only when every turn contains a well-formed Change-of-Meaning analysis.
Across four aligned victim models, PsychJail achieves the highest average attack success rate of 87.3%.
PsychJail outperforms strong single-turn and multi-turn baselines on every victim model.
The authors measure susceptibility at the action that breaks each victim model.
Measuring susceptibility at the breaking action reveals four distinct model-level fingerprints.
The model-level fingerprints identify which persuasion levers affect each model and how broadly.
The model-level fingerprints help explain cross-model transfer asymmetry.
The four model-level fingerprints may be interpreted as four candidate psychological profiles: rationalist, credibility-driven, narrative-mo
The interpretation of the four model-level fingerprints as psychological profiles is a conjecture that requires future validation.
The findings establish psychological jailbreaks as a distinct red-teaming frontier for increasingly interactive LLMs.
Google DeepMind's recent model DiffusionGemma (DG) generates text via diffusion.

claims.text: Decentralized, serverless learning increasingly connects devices running different architectures.
Decentralized SGD is undefined for models with different parameter counts because such models cannot be averaged.
Knowledge distillation exchanges soft predictions rather than weights.
Knowledge distillation sidesteps the obstacle that decentralized SGD is undefined for models with different parameter counts.
Convergence theory for fully decentralized, asynchronous peer-to-peer knowledge distillation is lacking.
The paper provides a convergence theory for fully decentralized, asynchronous peer-to-peer knowledge distillation.
The convergence theory relocates consensus from parameter space to function (output) space.
A knowledge distillation event is a geometric contraction operator in logit space on the peers' predictive distributions.
The knowledge distillation operator is analysed in the Hilbert space of predictions on a reference measure.
The convergence analysis relies on standard smoothness and variance assumptions.
The convergence analysis relies on two realizability assumptions: one bridging parameter SGD to the functional step, and one controlling res
Under these assumptions, the time-averaged functional stationarity converges at rate O(1/(ηT)) to an O(η)+O(Bf^2)+O(ζf^2) neighbourhood.
Bf is the distance from the task optimum to the peers' reachable classes.
Ζf measures persistent local-task heterogeneity.
Across homogeneous, width-heterogeneous, and mixed-family networks of the experiments, knowledge distillation contracts function disagreemen
Isolated training does not contract function disagreement across the experimental networks.
The sampled stationarity diagnostic has late transient exponents of 0.99-1.90 on the shared-skeleton main runs.
The four-point step-size sweep exhibits the predicted transient neighbourhood tradeoff.
Accurate segmentation of polyps and skin lesions is pivotal for clinical diagnosis.
Existing segmentation methods struggle with low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and cross-domain distribution discrepancies.
Discriminative networks predict standalone binary masks.
Existing segmentation approaches leave the visual priors of large-scale pretrained generative models largely unexploited.
InstEditSeg is a unified generative framework that reformulates medical segmentation as an instruction-driven image editing problem.
InstEditSeg renders a color-coded overlay on the original image, conditioned on a textual instruction, instead of emitting a mask.
The edited output of InstEditSeg aligns with the natural image distribution learned by latent diffusion models.
InstEditSeg mitigates the domain gap between natural and medical imagery.
InstEditSeg introduces DINOv3 as an auxiliary visual encoder to recover fine anatomical structures.
InstEditSeg introduces a DINO Feature Guidance Block that builds a multi-scale feature pyramid.
The multi-scale feature pyramid is fused into the diffusion U-Net by channel concatenation and zero-initialized convolution.
Hierarchical discriminative priors can be injected into the diffusion U-Net without perturbing the pretrained weights.
A dual-branch classifier-free guidance strategy reduces inference cost.
On polyp and skin lesion benchmarks, the InstEditSeg framework achieves accuracy competitive with strong discriminative baselines.
The InstEditSeg framework demonstrates better cross-domain generalization on unseen data than discriminative baselines.
The generative formulation of InstEditSeg yields more complete multi-lesion segmentation.
The generative formulation of InstEditSeg provides instruction-conditioned task control.
The generative formulation of InstEditSeg provides sampling flexibility.
The generative paradigm used by InstEditSeg has color sensitivity as a limitation.
The InstEditSeg code is available at https://github.com/wincharm001/InstEditSeg.
Multimodal Recommender Systems (MRSs) typically rely on a flawed "modality harmony" assumption.
The modality harmony assumption presumes that multimodal features are inherently beneficial.
Modality-topology conflicts are ubiquitous in real-world scenarios.
Modality-topology conflicts arise from deceptive visual clickbaits.
Blindly integrating noisy modalities inevitably pollutes the pristine collaborative space.
Blindly integrating noisy modalities causes severe representation distortion.
The authors propose OrthoRec, an orthogonal purification and topology-guided MoE approach for conflict-aware multimodal recommendation.
Collaborative-Guided Orthogonal Purification (CGOP) geometrically decouples multimodal features into directions parallel and orthogonal to a
CGOP adaptively truncates the orthogonal noise with an energy-preserving normalization.
CGOP rectifies deceptive semantic directions while preserving the modality's intrinsic representation capacity.
The authors design a Topology-Aware Routing Mixture-of-Experts (TAR-MoE).
TAR-MoE employs decoupled sigmoid gating to break the zero-sum bottleneck of traditional softmax attention.
TAR-MoE autonomously determines the injection scale for each purified modality.
TAR-MoE is guided by the collaborative topology.
A safe-SSL objective is introduced to dynamically penalize the forced contrastive alignment of contradictory pairs.
Experiments on three real-world Amazon datasets show that OrthoRec consistently outperforms competitive recent baselines.
OrthoRec exhibits improved robustness under modality noise.

claims.text: Practical uncertainty quantification for large language models must decide, from a single generation, whether a specific answer should be tr
Existing uncertainty quantification methods sample multiple generations.
ActMap is a white-box representation that compresses the generation-time hidden-state trajectory (every layer, every generated token) into a
The ActMap representation preserves structure across transformer depth and pooled hidden coordinates.
The ActMap is captured during the generation pass with no measurable overhead.
The ActMap has a fixed shape across model depths and hidden sizes.
An ActMap occupies 96 KiB.
An ActMap is a compact artifact that can be retained for audit-relevant generations and probed directly.
Occlusion analysis localizes the classifier's signal to mid-depth regions of the ActMap.
A lightweight classifier, instantiated as a compact Vision Transformer, reads an estimated correctness probability from each ActMap.
The lightweight classifier reads an estimated correctness probability from each ActMap in a fraction of a millisecond.
The ActMap representation itself carries the uncertainty result, rather than the classifier architecture.
ActMap is trained and evaluated in-domain on short-answer QA, direct-answer math, and summarization factuality.
ActMap is evaluated with three instruction-tuned 7-8B models.
ActMap consistently outperforms sampling, token-probability, attention, and embedding baselines.
ActMap matches ACT-ViT in mean AUROC.
ACT-ViT is a detector trained on dense activation tensors 67× larger than the ActMap input.
ActMap achieves lower calibration error than ACT-ViT on ten of twelve pairs.
The ActMap score supports abstention from a single generation.
ActMap is a practical primitive for scalable oversight of deployed models.

claims.text: In many enterprise settings, AI agents are provisioned the same as employee-owned hosts, with a static credential set fixed at deployment th
Role-based access control accepted this compromise for human principals because scoping access per task was infeasible.
For AI agents, static credential provisioning leaves every credential standing exposed whether or not the current task uses it.
The permissions of AI agents can later be utilised by a compromised or misaligned agent.
The problem of static permissions for AI agents is the task-context mismatch.
A three-source permission architecture, comprising role-based permission ceilings, a task permission classifier and policy-based prohibition
The three-source permission architecture eliminates the exposure preemptively.
Prior work released a 600-prompt labelled dataset for evaluating the three-source permission architecture.
The security gate is a fine-tuned RoBERTa-large encoder.
The fine-tuned RoBERTa-large encoder matched few-shot trained Claude Haiku 4.5 on classification quality.
The fine-tuned RoBERTa-large encoder achieved a macro-F1 of 0.881, compared with 0.886 for few-shot trained Claude Haiku 4.5.

The paper proposes an attack-surface elimination metric.
The role ceiling alone closes 27.9% of the severity-weighted attack surface.
Adding the task classifier to the role ceiling closes 84.4% of the severity-weighted attack surface.
Task-granular access control displays security advantages over role-granular access control.
AI agents are the first principal type for which task-granular access control is enforceable.
Task-granular access control is enforceable for AI agents because the tasks of AI agents arrive as machine-readable text.
The research establishes task-based access control as a measured mechanism for reducing attack surface in agentic deployments.
Task-based access control is potentially deployable as a mechanism for reducing attack surface in agentic deployments.
The authors present an efficient method to distill reasoning capabilities into compact video-language models (VLMs) for video question answe
The method fine-tunes a 2B-parameter model using only approximately 900 uncertainty-selected examples.
Each of the approximately 900 uncertainty-selected examples is augmented with synthetic chain-of-thought (CoT) rationales generated by a 4B
The method's training requires under two hours on a single A100 GPU.
The method's training has minimal compute cost.
The 2B-parameter model outperforms VLMs up to 4 times larger.
The 2B-parameter model generalizes across CinePile, ActivityNet-QA, and MLVU.
The 2B-parameter model approaches the performance of its own 4B teacher model.
Placing CoT rationales after the answer substantially improves reasoning in compact models.
Placing CoT rationales after the answer runs contrary to standard prompting.
The finding that placing CoT rationales after the answer improves reasoning challenges prevailing CoT conventions.
The finding reveals new alignment strategies under limited model capacity.
The findings offer a practical blueprint for training deployable, reasoning-rich VLMs suited for mobile and edge applications.

claims.text: Transformers and state-space models (SSMs) are the two dominant families of sequence models.
A central open question is how far the analytical knowledge built for transformers transfers to SSMs.
The authors address the question of how far transformer analysis transfers to SSMs through the lens of layer importance.
Layer importance underpins compression across transformers and SSMs.
The authors decompose layer importance into two distinct notions, Necessity and Plasticity.
Necessity captures how much the pretrained model depends on a layer's existing contribution.
Necessity is measured by the loss increase from bypassing a layer.
Plasticity captures where the model absorbs new information during fine-tuning.
Plasticity is measured by the magnitude of task-specific weight updates.
Transformers and SSMs behave fundamentally differently with respect to layer importance.
In every evaluated residual transformer up to 14B parameters, Necessity and Plasticity anti-align across depth.
In the evaluated Mamba-style SSMs, Necessity and Plasticity point to overlapping regions.
The sign of the alignment between Necessity and Plasticity predicts downstream adaptation behavior.
In the evaluated transformers, concentrating updates in the most plastic layers increases catastrophic forgetting.
The tier-dependent effect of concentrating updates in the most plastic layers disappears in the evaluated Mamba-style SSMs.

Alignment methods such as PPO, DPO, DIL, and GRPO have become popular post-training techniques.
Many papers show that alignment methods have a significant positive impact on model performance by punishing negative samples.
Alignment methods that punish negative samples keep training complexity acceptable.
Most alignment methods address simple single-turn tasks.

The authors propose Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation (tlm-DRE) as a training method.
Tlm-DRE assigns different weights to corresponding turns.
Tlm-DRE proposes asymmetric token-level training based on positive-negative space gaps across multiple turns of tasks.
Tlm-DRE performs competitively compared to traditional alignment methods on a wide range of agent benchmarks.

Interface compatibility alone does not establish capability retention.

The three calibration layers apply to every scenario.

Aggregate improvement on capability measures is a stronger objective than non-degradation.

Harness calibration aligns observable artifacts at semantic checkpoints.
Harness calibration repairs misaligned artifacts through iteration, tool substitution, or local replanning.

The authors propose held-out evaluations for model changes, cross-border adaptation, and scale.
The proposed held-out evaluations include a factorial test of source evidence and checkpoint repair.

Group-level reporting is intended to prevent aggregate gains from masking local failures.

claims.text: Rubric-based evaluation is widely used to assess large language model (LLM) outputs by decomposing quality into multiple criteria.

Judgment certainty varies substantially across criteria in rubric-based evaluation.
Existing methods uniformly aggregate criterion-level judgments into a final score.
Existing methods implicitly treat every criterion as equally certain.
Existing methods overlook the heterogeneity in judgment certainty across criteria.
Uncertain judgments remain incorporated into reward estimation without distinction.

URW elicits a soft uncertainty signal from a fixed pool of paraphrased judgment templates.
URW converts the soft uncertainty signal into a per-criterion weight using split-conformal p-values.
The split-conformal p-values used by URW come with provable coverage guarantees.
URW consistently improves pairwise preference accuracy.
URW delivers stronger downstream RL alignment.
